_comment: The words on each game's start page (wordlink.au/<slug>). tools/build-links.py reads this and writes the pages. name is the H1 and the game's name; seo is the <title>; meta is the search snippet; sub is the one line a learner reads; about, how, cls and good are the part below Play, written for teachers and tutors. Keep every page's text its own: search engines ignore a paragraph repeated across pages.

games.name: Letter Names
games.seo: Letter Names Game: Hear an English Letter and Tap It | Free Alphabet Practice for Adults
games.meta: Free alphabet game for adult English learners. Hear a letter name, tap the right letter. Printed and handwritten letters. No sign-up.
games.sub: Hear a letter name and choose the letter.
games.about: An alphabet listening game for adults learning English letters for the first time. The learner hears a letter name, like "G" or "J", and taps it from four letters. Some rounds show the letters handwritten instead of printed, so learners recognise both. Letters that sound alike, like B, D, P, E, G and V, come up often.
games.cls: Open the Teacher Game, choose Letter Names, and students join on their phones with the room code or QR code. The projector says the letter and everyone answers at once.

games.name: Big and Small Letters
games.seo: Big and Small Letters: Match Capital and Lowercase Letters | Free Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Match uppercase and lowercase letters, then write names with a capital letter. Free English literacy game for adults.
games.sub: Match big and small letters.
games.about: A matching game for uppercase and lowercase letters. The learner sees a capital letter and finds its small letter, or the other way round. Other rounds show a name in small letters, like "fatima", and ask the learner to write it with a capital at the start.
how: Tap its big or small partner.
In writing rounds, type the name with a capital letter.
games.cls: Choose Big and Small Letters in the Teacher Game. Students tap on their phones while the letter shows on the projector.

games.name: Beginner Sound Gap
games.seo: Beginner Sound Gap: CVC Word Families Phonics Game | Free Phonics for Adult Beginners
games.meta: Phonics game with CVC word families like -at, -an, -ig and -ot. Hear the word, tap the missing first sound. Free for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear the missing sound and tap it.
games.about: A first phonics game built on short CVC word families: -an, -at, -ap, -et, -en, -ig, -in, -ip, -op, -ot, -ug and -un. The learner hears a word like "cat", sees "_at" and taps the missing first sound. Every round stays in one rhyming family, so one sound decides the answer.
how: Look at the word with a gap.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Sound Gap in the Teacher Game. The projector shows the word family and students tap the sound on their phones.

games.name: Beginner Tap Word
games.seo: Beginner Tap Word: Read CVC Rhyming Words | Free Decoding Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear a short word and tap it from rhyming words like cat, bat, hat. A free decoding game for adults learning to read English.
games.sub: Hear a word and tap it.
games.about: A decoding game with short rhyming words. The learner hears "pen" and chooses from pen, hen, ten and men. The words differ by one sound, so the learner has to read the first letter, not guess. It uses the same word families as Beginner Sound Gap.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Tap Word in the Teacher Game. The word is spoken from the projector and students tap it on their phones.

games.name: Beginner Build Word
games.seo: Beginner Build Word: Build CVC Words From Sounds | Free Blending Game for Adults
games.meta: Put the sounds in order to build short words like man, pig and sun. Free phonics blending and segmenting game for adult learners.
games.sub: Build the word from its sounds.
games.about: A blending and segmenting game. The learner hears a short word and puts its sound tiles in order, like m, a, n for "man". Each tile plays its sound, recorded by a real voice. It is the step from hearing sounds to spelling words.
how: Tap or drag the sound tiles into order.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Build Word in the Teacher Game. Students build the word on their phones and the answers show on the projector.

games.name: Elementary Sound Gap
games.seo: Elementary Sound Gap: Digraphs and Vowel Teams Phonics Game | sh, ch, th, ee, ai, oa
games.meta: Phonics game for digraphs and vowel teams: sh, ch, th, wh, ph, ee, ea, ai, ay, oa, oo, ou. Hear the word, tap the missing sound.
games.sub: Hear the missing sound in a longer word.
games.about: The next step in phonics, built on two-letter sounds: consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh, ph) and vowel teams (ee, ea, ai, ay, oa, oe, ie, ue, oo, ou and more). The learner hears a word like "rain" and taps the missing sound. The words are from everyday life: ship, chips, phone, train, boat.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Sound Gap in the Teacher Game. It is a good way to revise one sound pattern with the whole class.
good: long vowel sounds ee ai oa

games.name: Elementary Tap Word
games.seo: Elementary Tap Word: Read Words With Digraphs and Vowel Teams | Free Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear a word and tap it from words with the same sound pattern, like boat, coat, road. Free English decoding game for adults.
games.sub: Hear a longer word and tap it.
games.about: A decoding game for words with digraphs and vowel teams. The four choices share a sound pattern, like moon, food, soon and pool, so the learner has to read the whole word.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Tap Word in the Teacher Game and students answer on their phones.

games.name: Elementary Build Word
games.seo: Elementary Build Word: Build Words From Sound Tiles (Graphemes) | Free Phonics for Adults
games.meta: Build words like ship, train and moon from grapheme tiles, where two letters can make one sound. Free phonics game for adults.
games.sub: Build a longer word from its sounds.
games.about: The learner builds words from sound tiles, not single letters: "ship" is sh, i, p and "train" is t, r, ai, n. It teaches that two letters can make one sound, which is the key to spelling longer English words.
how: Put the sound tiles in order.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Build Word in the Teacher Game. The projector shows everyone's answers, so mistakes are easy to talk about.

games.name: Sight Words
games.seo: Sight Words Game: Hear and Tap Common English Words | Free High-Frequency Words for Adults
games.meta: Hear a common word like the, was, have or would, and tap it. A free sight words and high-frequency words game for adults.
games.sub: The words you see everywhere.
games.about: A game for high-frequency sight words like the, and, you, was, have, come, would and little. Many of them cannot be sounded out, so learners need to know them by sight. The learner hears the word and taps it from four written words.
games.cls: Choose Sight Words in the Teacher Game for a quick warm-up.

games.name: Picture and Word
games.seo: Picture and Word: Match a Picture to Its English Word | Free Reading Game for Adults
games.meta: Look at a picture and tap its word. A free vocabulary and early reading game for adult English learners. No typing.
games.sub: Look at the picture and tap its word.
games.about: An early reading game where a picture carries the meaning. The learner sees a picture, like a bus or an apple, and taps its word from four written words. There is no typing, and the instruction is spoken.
how: Tap the word for the picture.
games.cls: Choose Picture and Word in the Teacher Game. The picture shows on the projector and students tap the word on their phones.

games.name: Read the Notice
games.seo: Read the Notice: Find the Date, Time and Price on a Notice | Free Reading Practice for Adults
games.meta: Read short notices like a class time, a shop closure or a bus timetable. Find what, when and how much. Free survival English reading.
games.sub: Find what a notice tells you.
games.about: A reading game with short everyday notices: an English class, a shop closed sign, a bus timetable, a doctor's appointment and a for sale sign. The learner answers one question: what is it about, when is it, or how much is it. It practises scanning for the key information.
games.cls: Choose Read the Notice in the Teacher Game, then ask the class where they see notices like these.

games.name: Copy It
games.seo: Copy It: Copy Words, Names and Numbers | Free Writing and Typing Practice for Adults
games.meta: Copy a word, a full name or a number exactly, with capitals in the right place. Free copying practice for adult literacy learners.
games.sub: Copy a word, a name or a number.
games.about: Copying practice for learners starting to write. Rounds take turns between a word (some with a picture), a full name like "Mai Nguyen" and a number. Capital letters must match, so learners practise writing names the way forms expect them.
how: Look at the word, name or number.
games.cls: Choose Copy It in the Teacher Game. It works well before a paper form activity.

games.name: Capitals and Full Stops
games.seo: Capitals and Full Stops: Punctuation Game for Adult English Learners | Free
games.meta: Choose the correctly written sentence, or add the capital letter and full stop. Free punctuation practice for adults.
games.sub: Start big, end with a full stop.
games.about: A punctuation game for the first two rules: a sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. Some rounds ask which of four sentences is written correctly. Others give a sentence in small letters to write again properly. The sentences are about everyday life, like "I live in Springvale."
how: Tap the right one, or write it correctly.
games.cls: Choose Capitals and Full Stops in the Teacher Game and go through the wrong answers together.
good: capital letters and full stops activity

games.name: Write a Sentence
games.seo: Write a Sentence About Yourself: Model Sentences for Adult English Learners | Free
games.meta: Follow a model like "My name is David. I am from Vietnam." and write two sentences about yourself. Free writing practice for adults.
games.sub: Write a sentence about you.
games.about: Guided writing from a model. The learner sees two model sentences, like "My name is David. I am from Vietnam.", and writes two sentences about themselves the same way. Topics are name and country, where you live, family, class day, language and work. Capitals and full stops count.
how: Change them to be about you.
games.cls: Choose Write a Sentence in the Teacher Game. Students' sentences show on the projector, which is a good start for speaking.

games.name: All Spelling
games.seo: All Spelling: Hear and Spell English Words From Every Topic | Free Spelling Game for Adults
games.meta: Mixed spelling game: numbers, days, months, weather, fruit, body and clothes words. Type it or choose it. Free for adult English learners.
games.sub: Spell words from every topic.
games.about: A mixed spelling review across the vocabulary topics: number words, days, months, weather, fruit, parts of the body and clothes. The learner hears a word and types it. Multiple choice is there for an easier round.
games.cls: Choose All Spelling in the Teacher Game for an end-of-week spelling quiz.

games.name: Days of the Week
games.seo: Days of the Week Game: Hear and Spell Monday to Sunday | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear a day of the week and spell it, with a capital letter. Free English vocabulary and spelling game for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear a day of the week and write it.
games.about: A listening and spelling game for the seven days, Monday to Sunday. Days start with a capital letter and the game marks that, so learners learn to write them properly. Multiple choice is there for learners who cannot type yet.
how: Type it with a capital letter.
games.cls: Choose Days of the Week in the Teacher Game, then ask "What day is today?"

games.name: Months
games.seo: Months of the Year Game: Hear and Spell January to December | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear a month and spell it, with a capital letter. Free months of the year spelling game for adult English learners.
games.sub: Hear a month and write it.
games.about: A listening and spelling game for the twelve months. Learners hear the month and type it with its capital letter. February, August and September are the usual hard ones.
how: Type it with a capital letter.
games.cls: Choose Months in the Teacher Game, then follow up with Find the Date.

games.name: Weather
games.seo: Weather Words Game: Sunny, Rainy, Windy, Humid | Free English Vocabulary for Adults
games.meta: Hear and spell weather words: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, stormy, foggy, hot, cold, warm, humid. Free ESL game for adults.
games.sub: Hear a weather word and write it.
games.about: Vocabulary and spelling for the weather: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, snowy, stormy, foggy, hot, cold, warm, cool and humid. These are the words for small talk and for reading a weather forecast. In multiple choice the learner taps the matching picture.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Weather in the Teacher Game, then ask "What is the weather like today?"

games.name: Fruits
games.seo: Fruit Names Game: Hear and Spell Fruits in English | Free Vocabulary for Adult Learners
games.meta: Apple, banana, mango, watermelon and more. Hear a fruit name and spell it, or tap its picture. Free English game for adults.
games.sub: Hear the fruit and write its name.
games.about: Fruit vocabulary for shopping: apple, banana, orange, grape, mango, peach, plum, pear, lemon, cherry, strawberry, watermelon, pineapple, coconut and kiwi. The learner hears the word and spells it, or in multiple choice taps the matching picture.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Fruits in the Teacher Game, and follow up with Shop or Read the List.

games.name: Parts of the Body
games.seo: Parts of the Body Game: Head, Knee, Wrist, Stomach | Free English for the Doctor
games.meta: Hear and spell 24 parts of the body, from head to toe. Free English vocabulary for adults, useful at the doctor or chemist.
games.sub: Hear a part of the body and write it.
games.about: Body vocabulary with clear drawings: head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, tooth, tongue, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, wrist, hand, finger, thumb, chest, stomach, back, hip, leg, knee, ankle, foot and toe. These are the words for telling a doctor where it hurts.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Parts of the Body in the Teacher Game, then practise "My ... hurts."
good: parts of the body for adults

games.name: Clothes
games.seo: Clothes Vocabulary Game: Jumper, Thongs, Beanie, Hoodie | Free Australian English for Adults
games.meta: Hear and spell 34 clothing words, including Australian ones like jumper, thongs and singlet. Free ESL vocabulary for adults.
games.sub: Hear the clothing word and write it.
games.about: Clothes and accessories with drawings, including Australian English words: shirt, jumper, jacket, coat, pants, jeans, shorts, singlet, hoodie, socks, shoes, boots, sandals, thongs, hat, cap, beanie, helmet, scarf, gloves, belt, glasses, watch, wallet, backpack, umbrella and more.
how: Type it, or tap the picture.
games.cls: Choose Clothes in the Teacher Game, then pair it with Weather: "It is cold. Wear a jumper."

games.name: Odd One Out
games.seo: Odd One Out Picture Game: Find the One That Does Not Belong | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Four pictures, three belong together. Animals, fruit, transport, clothes, food, weather, colours and more. Free ESL game for adults.
games.sub: Find the word that does not belong.
games.about: A picture game for grouping words by meaning. The learner sees four pictures, three from one group (animals, fruit, transport, clothes, body, food, weather, colours, numbers or actions), and taps the one that is different. It builds vocabulary in categories.
how: Find the one that is different.
games.cls: Choose Odd One Out in the Teacher Game, then ask students to say why.

games.name: Beginner Listen and Fill Gaps
games.seo: Beginner Listening Game: Hear a Sentence and Fill the Gap | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear simple sentences about you, like "I live in Springvale.", and write the missing word. Free listening practice for adults.
games.sub: Listen to a sentence and fill the gaps.
games.about: A listening gap-fill with short personal sentences, like "My ___ is David.", "I am ___ Vietnam." and "I go to English ___ three days a week." The learner hears the whole sentence and types the missing word, or taps it in multiple choice. The audio can be played again.
how: Type or tap the missing word.
games.cls: Choose Beginner Listen and Fill Gaps in the Teacher Game. The projector reads the sentence aloud to the whole room.

games.name: Elementary Listen and Fill Gaps
games.seo: Elementary Listening Game: Fill the Gap in Longer Sentences | Free English for Adults
games.meta: Hear longer everyday sentences and write the missing word. Free listening and gap-fill practice for adult English learners.
games.sub: Listen to a longer sentence and fill the gaps.
games.about: A listening gap-fill with longer sentences, like "She ___ at the fish shop on the main street." The sentences use the Elementary sound patterns (sh, ee, oo, ai), so listening and phonics go together. The learner types the missing word, or taps it in multiple choice.
how: Type or tap the missing word.
games.cls: Choose Elementary Listen and Fill Gaps in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Listen and Unscramble
games.seo: Listen and Unscramble: Hear a Sentence, Put the Words in Order | Free Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear a sentence, then drag the word tiles into order. Sentences about name, family, home and daily routine. Free ESL game.
games.sub: Listen, then put the words in order.
games.about: A listening and word order game. The learner hears a sentence, like "I have one son and one daughter.", then puts the mixed-up word tiles in order. The sentences cover personal information, family, home, daily routine and the weekend. In multiple choice the learner taps the sentence in the right order.
how: Tap or drag the words into order.
games.cls: Choose Listen and Unscramble in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Greetings
games.seo: Greetings Game: Hello, How Are You, Thank You | Free English Listening for Adult Beginners
games.meta: Hear a greeting or a question like "Where are you from?" and tap the right reply. Free everyday English for adults.
games.sub: Hear a greeting and answer it.
games.about: Everyday exchanges for the first weeks of English. The learner hears a greeting or courtesy phrase, like "How are you?", "Thank you." or "See you next week.", and taps the right reply. Other rounds ask short personal questions: "What is your name?", "Where are you from?", "How old are you?"
how: Listen to what the person says.
games.cls: Choose Greetings in the Teacher Game, then have students say the replies to each other.

games.name: Do What It Says
games.seo: Do What It Says: Follow Simple Spoken Instructions | Free English Listening for Adults
games.meta: Hear "Tap the book", "Open the door" or "Turn the sound off" and tap the right picture. Free listening game for adults.
games.sub: Listen, then tap what it says.
games.about: A game for following short spoken instructions. Classroom rounds use everyday things: "Tap the book.", "Open the door.", "Tap the cup." Device rounds use phone instructions: "Turn the sound off.", "Charge the battery.", "Take a photo." Every answer has a picture.
games.cls: Choose Do What It Says in the Teacher Game, then do the same instructions for real in the room.

games.name: Speaking Game
games.seo: Speaking Practice Game: Answer Everyday Questions in English | Free for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear a question like "What did you do on Saturday?" and build the answer from word tiles. Free English speaking preparation for adults.
games.sub: Hear the question and build your answer.
games.about: Practice for common conversation questions. The learner hears a question, like "Where do you live?", "What is your favourite food?", "Can you drive?" or "How was your weekend?", and builds a full answer from word tiles, like "On Saturday, I stayed at home." The answer is read aloud afterwards so the learner can say it too. In multiple choice the learner taps the right answer instead. To record their own voice, learners can use Speaking Practice on the home page.
how: Put the word tiles in order to make the answer.
Hear the answer and say it.
games.cls: Choose Speaking Game in the Teacher Game, then ask each student the same question aloud.

games.name: Question Words
games.seo: Question Words Game: What, Where, How, Who | Free English Grammar for Adults
games.meta: Choose the right question word for everyday questions like "___ old are you?" and "___ do you live?". Free ESL grammar game.
games.sub: Choose the right question word.
games.about: A reading game for question words. The learner sees an everyday question with its first word missing, like "___ is your name?" or "___ do you spell your name?", and taps or writes the right question word. These are the questions asked at enrolment, at the doctor and at work.
games.cls: Choose Question Words in the Teacher Game, then have pairs ask each other the questions.

games.name: Grammar Unscramble
games.seo: Grammar Unscramble: Put English Words in the Right Order | Free Sentence Game for Adults
games.meta: Drag the word tiles into a correct sentence, like "I live in a three-bedroom house." Free English word order practice for adults.
games.sub: Put the words in the right order.
games.about: A word order game with no audio. The learner sees the words of a sentence mixed up and puts them in order. The sentences are about personal information, family, home and daily routine, so they are useful for speaking and writing about yourself.
how: Tap or drag them into order.
games.cls: Choose Grammar Unscramble in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Translate
games.seo: Translate to English: Arabic, Dari, Persian, Pashto, Vietnamese, Chinese and More | Free
games.meta: Read a sentence in your language and write it in English. Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Dari, Hindi, Khmer, Pashto, Persian, Thai, Urdu, Vietnamese.
games.sub: Read it in your language, write it in English.
games.about: A translation game for learners who can read their first language. The learner reads a sentence in Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Dari, Hindi, Khmer, Pashto, Persian, Thai, Urdu or Vietnamese and writes it in English. In multiple choice they choose the right English sentence. The sentences are about name, family, home, daily routine and the weekend.
how: Write it in English, or tap it.
games.cls: Choose Translate in the Teacher Game. Each student picks their own language on their phone.

games.name: Numbers 1 to 10
games.seo: Number Words 1 to 10: Hear and Spell One to Ten | Free English Numbers for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number and spell its word: one, two, three... ten. Type it or choose it. Free English number words game for adults.
games.sub: Hear a number from 1 to 10 and spell it.
games.about: A spelling game for the number words one to ten. The learner hears the number and types the word, like "seven" or "eight". Multiple choice is there for learners who cannot type yet.
games.cls: Choose Numbers 1 to 10 in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Numbers 11 to 20
games.seo: Number Words 11 to 20: Thirteen or Thirty? | Free English Numbers Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear and spell eleven to twenty, the hardest English numbers to hear and spell. Free number words game for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear a number from 11 to 20 and spell it.
games.about: A spelling game for eleven to twenty. The teen numbers are hard to hear and hard to spell: twelve, fifteen, eighteen. The learner hears the number and types the word.
games.cls: Choose Numbers 11 to 20 in the Teacher Game, and point out the stress in thirTEEN and THIRty.

games.name: Numbers 21 to 99
games.seo: Number Words 21 to 99: Hear and Spell Twenty-One to Ninety-Nine | Free for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number and spell it with its hyphen, like forty-two. Free English number words game for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear a number from 21 to 99 and spell it.
games.about: A spelling game for two-digit number words, like twenty-one, forty-two and ninety-nine. Learners practise the tens words and the hyphen, which they need for forms and for writing amounts in words.
games.cls: Choose Numbers 21 to 99 in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Tap the Number
games.seo: Tap the Number: Hear a Number and Find It | Free Number Recognition Game for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number and tap it from four. The choices are close, like 13 and 31. Free number recognition game for adult learners.
games.sub: Hear a number and tap it.
games.about: A number recognition game with no typing. The learner hears a number and taps it from four numbers. The wrong choices are close (one more, one less, ten more, or the digits swapped), so the learner has to listen carefully.
games.cls: Choose Tap the Number in the Teacher Game as a quick warm-up.

games.name: Write the Number
games.seo: Write the Number: Write Numbers and Australian Money in Figures | Free for Adults
games.meta: Hear a number or price and write it in figures, or write what an Australian coin or note is worth. Free numeracy for adults.
games.sub: Write numbers and money in figures.
games.about: Writing numbers and money in figures. Rounds mix four kinds: write a number you hear, copy a number, write what an Australian coin or note is worth (from 5c to $50), and write an amount of money you hear, like $4.50.
how: Listen, or look at the coin or note.
games.cls: Choose Write the Number in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Add It Up
games.seo: Add It Up: Simple Addition in English | Free Numeracy Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear and read a simple sum like 4 + 3, then type the answer. Free numeracy and maths English for adults.
games.sub: Add two numbers together.
games.about: Simple addition, asked in English. The sum is spoken ("What is four plus three?") and shown on screen. The maths is easy on purpose: the aim is understanding numbers and "plus" in English.
games.cls: Choose Add It Up in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Add the Money
games.seo: Add the Money: Add Two Amounts in Dollars | Free Money Maths for Adult English Learners
games.meta: Hear "What is five dollars plus three dollars?" and type the total. Free money and numeracy game for adults.
games.sub: Add two amounts of money.
games.about: Adding two amounts of money in whole dollars. The question is spoken and shown, like "$5 + $3 = ?". It practises the word "dollars" and working out a total when shopping.
games.cls: Choose Add the Money in the Teacher Game, then follow with Shop.

games.name: Put In Order
games.seo: Put In Order: Order Numbers, Australian Money, Days and Months | Free Game for Adults
games.meta: Drag numbers, coins and notes, days or months into order. Free ordering and sequencing game for adult English learners.
games.sub: Put numbers, money, days and months in order.
games.about: An ordering game with four kinds of rounds: numbers from smallest to biggest, Australian coins and notes from smallest to biggest, three days of the week in order, and three months in order.
how: Tap or drag them into order.
games.cls: Choose Put In Order in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Tens and Ones
games.seo: Tens and Ones: Place Value Game for Adult Learners | Free Numeracy in English
games.meta: How many tens in 47? How many ones? Free place value game for adult numeracy and English learners.
games.sub: How many tens and how many ones.
games.about: A place value game for the numbers 11 to 99. The learner sees a number and answers "How many tens?" or "How many ones?". The question is spoken as well as shown.
games.cls: Choose Tens and Ones in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Read the List
games.seo: Read the List: Find Prices on a Price List | Free Shopping English for Adults
games.meta: Read a short price list, find how much something costs, and spot the cheaper item. Free reading and numeracy for adults.
games.sub: Find a price in a list.
games.about: A price list reading game, like a menu or a shop board. Rounds ask "How much is the bread?", "Which one is cheaper?" or "Which one is more expensive?". The items are everyday groceries at believable prices.
games.cls: Choose Read the List in the Teacher Game.

games.name: Find the Date
games.seo: Find the Date: Read a Calendar in English | Free Calendar Game for Adult Learners
games.meta: Read a month calendar: what day is May 14? Which month is this? Free calendar reading practice for adults.
games.sub: Find a day and a date on a calendar.
games.about: Calendar reading with a real month grid. The learner answers "What day is May 14?" by finding the date and reading its column, or answers "Which month is this?". It is practice for appointments, rent and school dates.
games.cls: Choose Find the Date in the Teacher Game. The calendar shows big on the projector.

games.name: First, Second, Third
games.seo: First, Second, Third: Ordinal Numbers Game | Free English for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear "Tap second" or "Tap the second one", or say which one is marked. Free ordinal numbers game for adult English learners.
games.sub: Which one is first, second or third.
games.about: Ordinal numbers with a row of people. The learner hears "Tap second." and chooses 2nd, hears "Tap the second one." and taps the second of 1, 2 and 3, or sees one person marked and names the position. These are the words for queues, floors and dates.
games.cls: Choose First, Second, Third in the Teacher Game, then line up the class for real.

games.name: Ordinal Numbers
games.seo: Ordinal Numbers 1st to 30th: Listening Game | Free English for Adult Learners
games.meta: Hear "Tap twenty-first" and choose 21st, or find the marked number and name it. Free game for ordinal numbers first to thirtieth.
games.sub: First to thirtieth.
games.about: Ordinal numbers from first to thirtieth, the way dates are said. The learner hears "Tap twelfth." and chooses 12th, hears "Tap the twelfth one." and taps 12 from numbers in counting order, or sees one number marked on a grid of 1 to 30 and chooses its word. The wrong options are the ones people mix up: thirteenth and thirtieth, twelfth and twentieth.
games.cls: Choose Ordinal Numbers in the Teacher Game, then say the dates of this month's classes aloud.

games.name: Where Is It
games.seo: Where Is It: Up, Down, Left, Right, In Front, Behind | Free English Game for Adults

games.sub: Up, down, left, right, in front, behind.
games.about: Direction and position words. The learner sees an arrow and answers which way it points (up, down, left or right), or sees a person and a box and answers whether the box is in front or behind.

games.name: Clock
games.seo: Interactive Clock Game: Move the Hour and Minute Hands | Free Telling Time for Adults
games.meta: Drag the clock hands to set the time, and read analogue clocks. O'clock, half past, quarter past, quarter to, 5 minutes. Free.
games.sub: Read the clock and set the time.
games.about: An interactive analogue clock with hour and minute hands you can drag. Rounds take turns: read the clock and choose the time, then set the clock to a time, like "Set the clock to 3:15, quarter past three". It moves from o'clock to half past, then quarter past and quarter to, then 5-minute steps. The wrong choices are the real mistakes, like reading the hands the wrong way round.
how: Read the clock and tap the time.
Drag the hour and minute hands to the time shown.
games.cls: Choose Clock in the Teacher Game. The clock shows big on the projector and every student sets the hands on their own phone.

how: Tap coins and notes to pay.
games.cls: Choose Shop in the Teacher Game. Every student pays on their phone and the projector shows who got it right.

games.name: Dice

games.sub: Roll two dice and get closest to the target.
games.about: A dice game for adding and deciding. The learner rolls two dice, adds them to their score and types the new score, then chooses to roll again or stop. Going over the target means you are out. You choose the target number, and whether a wrong sum ends your game or gives one more try.
how: Roll the dice and type your new score.
Get closest to the target without going over.
games.cls: Choose Dice in the Teacher Game. The whole class races to the target on the projector and the closest score wins.

games.name: Security
games.seo: Security: What Not to Share Online | Free Scam Awareness and Digital Safety for Adults
games.meta: Can you share your PIN? Your first name? Learn what to keep private, and copy a verification code. Free.
games.sub: Copy a code, and what to keep private.
games.about: Online safety with yes or no answers. The learner decides whether something is safe to share, like a first name, a class day or a favourite colour, or must stay private, like a bank PIN, a password, a card number or a photo of a passport. Other rounds practise copying a 4-digit code, like a verification code sent by SMS.
how: Decide if you can share it.
Tap yes or no, or type the code.
games.cls: Choose Security in the Teacher Game, then talk about scams before setting up banking or myGov apps.
